title: Dark Web Monitoring
summary: Dark web monitoring is the systematic collection and analysis of content from sources that mainstream search engines do not index, including criminal forums, illicit marketplaces, paste sites, private messaging channels, ransomware leak sites and credential dumps, in order to detect exposure, fraud enablers and threats to an organisation. For defenders it supports four main use cases: discovering leaked or stolen credentials and session material before it is used, identifying brand impersonation and phishing infrastructure, learning about planned or ongoing campaigns that name the organisation or its suppliers, and gathering adversary tradecraft that can be turned into detection. Collection is harder than it first appears. Sources are ephemeral and hostile, registration often requires vouching or payment, access carries legal, contractual and personal safety risk, and much of the content is recycled, fabricated or seeded by criminals and by researchers themselves. Verification is therefore the core analyst skill: a credential listing proves nothing until a controlled check confirms it is current, and a forum post claiming an intrusion may simply be a sales pitch. Sound programmes use dedicated isolated collection environments, maintain strict separation between collection identities and corporate infrastructure, operate under rules of engagement approved by legal and leadership, and handle material that may contain personal data in line with privacy regulation. Output is only valuable when it reaches a workflow, so mature teams route validated findings into identity remediation, takedown requests, fraud monitoring and intelligence reporting, and they record which sources produced results and which produced noise.
objectives: You will be able to define collection requirements that connect dark web monitoring to specific defensive decisions.
You will be able to explain the legal, privacy and personal safety constraints that govern covert collection and reporting.
You will be able to validate leaked credential and access listings before triggering remediation or escalation.
You will be able to distinguish genuine exposure from recycled, fabricated or researcher-seeded content.
You will be able to route validated findings into identity, fraud, takedown and intelligence workflows.
You will be able to measure source productivity and retire collection that generates noise without decisions.

sources.label: NIST Computer Security Resource Center publications

beginner.definition: Dark web monitoring means watching hidden online places for signs that your organisation has been exposed. These places include criminal forums, marketplaces and leak sites that normal search engines do not list. The goal is to find stolen passwords or plans against you early. Then you can act before the attacker does.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stolen passwords are often sold long before anyone uses them. If you find them first, you can reset them and lock the account. That removes an easy way in. Monitoring also reveals fake websites that copy your brand to trick customers. Ignoring all this leaves you blind. You may learn about a leak only when a criminal logs in, which is far too late.
howItWorks: Set a clear question first. Decide what you want to learn, such as leaked staff logins.
Collect carefully, using isolated machines and research identities that stay away from work accounts.
Treat everything as untrusted. Much of this content is old, copied, fake or planted by other researchers.
Verify before you act. Check whether a leaked password still works, using an approved and safe process.
Route real findings to the right team, such as identity, fraud or legal, with a deadline.
Record which sources gave useful results, and stop paying for the ones that only make noise.
beginner.example: Imagine you lose your wallet. Someone finds it and sells your bank card details to a stranger online. You do not know yet, and nothing bad has happened. A monitoring service is like a friend who watches those market stalls. They see your card listed and tell you at once. You call the bank and cancel the card before anyone spends your money. That early warning is the whole value.
takeaways: Find stolen credentials early so you can reset them before an attacker logs in.
Treat dark web content as unverified, because much of it is old or fake.
Only collect within agreed rules, and keep your research identity away from work systems.

exercises.title: Dark Web Monitoring - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Dark Web Monitoring - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Dark Web Monitoring - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Dark Web Monitoring - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
